title: ⸸ P034 — XHTML Attributes Must Have Explicit Values
description: XHTML specification requires all attributes to have explicit values. Boolean HTML5 attributes like 'checked', 'disabled', 'selected', and 'readonly' must be written as attribute="attribute" in XHTML (e.g., 'checked="checked"') instead of bare attribute names (e.g., 'checked'). Failure to do so causes XHTML parser errors: 'Specification mandates value for attribute <name>'.
detectionNotes: Bare boolean attributes appear as standalone tokens followed by whitespace or />
This is valid HTML5 but invalid XHTML strict mode
Scanner must exclude these attributes when found inside CDATA sections
Scanner must exclude these attributes when found inside HTML/JavaScript comments

2026-05-25-checklist.status: NO BARE ATTRIBUTES (uses CDATA for JavaScript)

relatedIssues: XHTML validation error: xmlParseEntityRef: no name (when unescaped && in script)
XHTML validation error: Specification mandates value for attribute <name>
preventionStrategies: Use automated XHTML validator (xmllint, online validators) in CI pipeline
Use IDE extensions for XHTML validation (e.g., VS Code XHTML Validator)
Search-and-replace patterns for all XHTML files during creation/modification
Code review checklist: verify all boolean attributes have explicit values
Use template snippets in IDE that generate correct XHTML syntax
